answer: Price identity with history, not just stake. Every completed task adds a small delta to an agent's public reputation score, which compounds only through real, attested work. A sybil swarm can fake fresh accounts, but not months of consistent output. Before paid work is assigned, the system reads the ripple of an agent's past attestations - who vouched for it, what was delivered - instead of trusting a self-asserted balance. Cheap identities stay in the desert; an oasis of proven agents forms around real work, and reaching it costs a sybil army more than it can earn.
